intro.heading: Open your home to a future ministry leader.
intro.text: A healthy, stable place to live is a big part of a resident's growth. Our host families give residents a private room, a safe home, and a front-row seat to everyday faith. Would you prayerfully consider hosting a resident?
intro.photoAlt: Two people laughing together at an outdoor CCC gathering

stability.heading: Why one to three years?
stability.text: Instead of moving residents every few months, we ask hosts to commit to one to three years. Long-term stability is better for the resident's development, and it gives you time to build a real relationship.

items.title: What residents and host families say

hosts.heading: What we ask of host families.

items.title: Pray and agree
items.text: Listen to the Holy Spirit about whether this is right for your family. If you're married, you and your spouse should both be fully on board.

items.title: Provide a private space
items.text: A private bedroom with standard furnishings, plus a private or semi-private bathroom. A basement, mother-in-law suite, or guest house works too.

items.title: Keep a clean, safe home
items.text: Not spotless all the time. Generally clean and secure, so the resident feels comfortable and safe.

items.title: Host free of charge
items.text: Don't expect payment for rent and utilities. It removes a major cost for the resident and helps the church financially.

items.title: Have reliable Wi-Fi
items.text: Residents take online courses through Crown College, so a stable internet connection is required.

items.title: Communicate early
items.text: Talk through house rules, boundaries, and expectations in the first few days.

items.title: Connect relationally
items.text: Invite them to a meal or out for coffee. None of it is required, and both your boundaries and theirs are respected.

residents.heading: What residents commit to
points: Respect your personal space and house rules
Follow the same code of conduct as CCC staff
Clean up after themselves in private and shared spaces
Offer to help with light tasks like trash, vacuuming, or shoveling snow
Provide their own groceries, meals, and transportation

staff.heading: How the residency team supports you
points: Sets expectations and boundaries with both host and resident
Provides mediation and conflict resolution when needed
Checks in quarterly and hosts two host family gatherings each year
Finds another home for the resident if the need ever arises

steps.heading: How to become a host family.

items.title: Read the host family guide
items.text: It covers everything involved, including a communication guide to work through as a family.

items.title: Apply online
items.text: One member of the household fills out the host family application on Church Center.

items.title: Complete a background check
items.text: Every adult living in the home completes one. We ask the same of every incoming resident.

items.title: Schedule a home visit
items.text: A member of the residency team will walk through the space with you, in person or virtually.

steps.note: Want to talk with a current or former host family first? [Send us a note](/apply/#contact) and we'll connect you.

support.heading: Not able to host? You can still help.
support.text: Each month, residents raise their own financial support, and the church matches donations up to $400 per month per resident. Partner with a resident by giving online.
